title: Compute the knapsack bound by hand

blocks.text: A retail chain picks which shop refits to fund from one budget. Some refits are ordered by a safety inspector (`must_do`). Before running a solver, its analyst wants the ceiling on what any plan can be worth, computed without one.
Write `fractional_bound(projects, budget)` in `bound.py`. It returns the optimal value of this LP relaxation, with $`P`$ the projects and $`M`$ the must-do ones:

Compute it by hand, with no solver: pay for every must-do project in full; then go through the other projects in decreasing order of $`\text{value}_i / \text{cost}_i`$, funding each one whole while it fits; the first that does not fit gets the share $`\text{room} / \text{cost}_i`$ that the remaining room buys, and you stop. The tests' must-do projects always fit the budget, and their ratios are all different.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from bound import Project, fractional_bound

# Four kitchen refits; the one in Leeds is ordered by the inspector.
refits = [
    Project("Leeds", 25, 40, must_do=True),
    Project("York", 20, 50),
    Project("Hull", 40, 60),
    Project("Bath", 10, 12),
]

print("bound at budget 85:", fractional_bound(refits, 85))
print("bound at budget 65:", fractional_bound(refits, 65))
print("bound at budget 25:", fractional_bound(refits, 25))

    must_do: bool = False

    """The LP relaxation's value for one budget row: must-dos, then best value per dollar, then a share."""
    # TODO: pay for the must-do projects, then fund the others best value per dollar first,
    # and take the share that fits of the first one that does not fit whole.
    return 0.0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    shops = [Project("A", 30, 60), Project("B", 40, 56), Project("C", 50, 55), Project("D", 20, 18)]
    print(fractional_bound(shops, 120), fractional_bound(shops, 100))

cases.says: with a budget that whole projects fill exactly, the bound is their total value
the first project that does not fit whole adds the share of its value that the room left buys
projects are taken in order of value per dollar, so a large valuable project can wait
must-do projects are paid for in full before any other, even with a poor ratio
